results.content: Joanne Hsu, director of the University of Michigan Surveys of Consumers, said sentiment fell across the political spectrum, with Republicans recording the steepest month-to-month drop. "Sentiment among Republicans is now 19% below readings just prior to the Iran conflict and the lowest since the 2024 election," Hsu said in a statement. Notably large declines were also recorded among older consumers, lower-income consumers, and those without a college degree — groups Hsu described as [...] The decline was broad-based. By the numbers: Since February, Republican consumer sentiment has plunged 15.1 index points, from 97.1 to 82, according to the latest University of Michigan Surveys of Consumers data. Democratic sentiment has fallen just 1.6 index points, from 41.8 to 40.2.

Republican consumer sentiment fell 15.1 points from February to August 2026, while Democratic sentiment fell 1.6 points over the same period.
